reasons: This SAE is published as a NumPy archive (params.npz), as Gemma Scope's first release is. Logogram reads SAE parameters only from safetensors files; Gemma Scope 2 is published as safetensors.
Its weights are a PyTorch pickle (a .pt file), which Logogram never opens: loading a pickle can run code hidden in it. Logogram reads SAEs only from safetensors files.
This SAE rescales its inputs by a factor measured on its training data (normalize_activations: expected_average_only_in), which its files don't hold, so Logogram can't reproduce it exactly.

This SAE reads blocks.0.hook_resid_mid, which Logogram can't map to a residual stream, an attention output, the attention heads' outputs (z) or an MLP output. SAEs on the stream between attention and MLP aren't supported yet.

This SAE is in Llama Scope's format (hyperparams.json and checkpoints/final.safetensors), which Logogram doesn't read yet.
This SAE is in OpenMOSS's format (config.json beside sae_weights.safetensors, as in Llama Scope R1), which Logogram doesn't read yet.

SAELens's registry reads this SAE (mistral-7b-res-wg, blocks.8.hook_resid_pre) with normalize_activations = 'constant_norm_rescale', which its own configuration doesn't state, so its files alone don't say what it computes.

These transcoders are published as one safetensors file per layer, configured at the top of their repository (circuit-tracer's format, which SAELens converts), a format Logogram doesn't read yet.

This is a cross-layer transcoder or crosscoder (its parameters are split by layer): it reads or writes several layers at once, which Logogram doesn't support yet. Choose an SAE or a single-layer transcoder.
Its weights are a PyTorch pickle (a .pth file), which Logogram never opens: loading a pickle can run code hidden in it. Logogram reads SAEs only from safetensors files.
This is a temporal SAE (conf.yaml): its features also read earlier tokens through attention, so it isn't an SAE of one activation, which is what Logogram reproduces.
